observations.seen: Each court preset sets a clear mood: dusk purple at Rucker, warm low sun in frame 3, blue night in frame 4. The players get flat fill with little key-to-rim separation, and frame 2's gym reads as an evenly lit olive wash with no flood direction.
Frame 3 casts long directional shadows from players and the hoop pole. In frames 1, 2 and 4 the players sit on faint blobs or have no visible contact shadow, so feet look pasted onto the floor.

Frame 4 shows screen-space reflections of the lamp posts and players on a glossy blue floor, plus a specular streak. The other frames have matte, unreflective courts, and the character skin and cloth show no environment response.

The frame 3 skyline is flat purple boxes with rectangular window decals and blown white gaps between them. The bleachers are untextured stepped slabs. The frame 2 gym is mostly hidden by blur. The trophy and ball cart are the only props with real detail.
Frame 4 has faint rain streaks and frame 2 has floating dust specks. None of the frames show indoor haze or volumetric light, and depth separation comes from DOF rather than atmosphere.

The court surfaces are single flat colors with no wear, wood grain or paint texture. Clothing is uniform matte color with no folds. The frame 4 tower has a noisy blue glass texture that clashes with the rest of the scene.

Characters are low-detail stylized figures with uncanny faces and identical builds. Court lines are broken into misaligned segments, and stray white hook shapes float near players' feet. The pixel-block lettering on the floor in frames 2 and 4 looks aliased.

Ten players are spread in a flat row with no focal grouping. The hoop is cropped at the top-right edge in frames 2 to 4 and at the top of frame 1. Large empty floor fills the lower third, and the court subject runs well past the 25–40% target.

The camera is low and close, roughly 20–30° above the floor with a wide perspective. That misses the elevated broadcast angle near 70° at FOV 40 the recipe calls for, and frame 1 crowds the players into the lens.

Film grain is visible in frame 1. Frame 2 uses heavy background DOF bokeh, and frame 4 has mild bloom on the lamps. The look holds up as tasteful but generic and does not reach the arena-fight grade the recipe specifies.
Most players stand in stiff idle poses with arms angled out and identical stances. Frame 3 shows a crouch to pick up the ball, but the frame 1 walk poses look rigid and have no foot planting.
The scoreboard, stamina bar, court tag and control strip are clean and on-theme with orange and cyan accents. The top mode and court bar is dense debug-style chrome that competes with the scene.
